A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RND-DAgger study. Their main text, algorithms, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support matching retained, relocated, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on RaceCar, HalfCheetah, and Maze, human-expert RaceCar experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds MET-augmented baseline experiments and total expert-time comparisons.

M1.justification: RND-DAgger retains the same prediction-error intervention criterion, consecutive in-distribution window, dataset aggregation, and training procedure. The stability window is renamed Minimal Expert Time (MET); its mechanism is unchanged. New MET-augmented comparators are baseline changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RaceCar, HalfCheetah, and Maze tasks, including human-expert RaceCar experiments. The additional MET and timing analyses use this existing coverage. Pixel observations and partial observability are discussed only as future extensions.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds Lazy-DAgger+MET and Ensemble-DAgger+MET as evaluated comparators; the latter also appears in the new expert-time comparison. The original oracle-comparison methods and human-experiment HG-DAgger baseline remain.

E3.justification: The main evaluation settings and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged. New MET comparisons search W using the existing RND-DAgger grid, and Table 5 introduces expert-action accounting with explicit frame-rate conversions. v1's supplementary hyperparameter selections for matched or best context-switch counts are removed.

E4.justification: The original HalfCheetah component ablation is retained, while Appendix C.2 substantially extends MET testing to both competing intervention methods across all three tasks. RaceCar visualizations now compare these methods with and without MET. Conversely, v1's matched-switch and best-switch analyses in Appendix D disappear.

E5.justification: v2 adds numerical ± uncertainty values to the existing results in Tables 1 and 3. Both versions already report eight seeded runs and show shaded plot bands. The revision does not specify what the ± quantities represent or establish increased run counts or a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains all task-performance means but revises Lazy-DAgger's RaceCar switches from 20,990 to 3,437 and Ensemble-DAgger's RaceCar/HalfCheetah switches from 18,391/13,883 to 2,785/1,452. Tables 4–5 add MET outcomes and expert-time estimates, while the old matched/best-switch curves are removed. New Table 4 reports Lazy-DAgger's Maze performance as 0.590, conflicting with 0.575 in v2 Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces the POMDP formulation, observation distribution, and history-conditioned policy with an MDP formulation and a current-state policy. This narrows the formal assumptions rather than merely changing notation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same central claims: state-based RND intervention detection, evaluation on three tasks, competitive task performance, and reduced expert burden. The added experiments support these existing claims rather than introduce a new headline contribution.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds specific limitations concerning immediate expert takeover, partial observability, and distracting high-entropy observations. Appendix C.2 explains that MET combined with baseline intervention rules can leave the expert continually controlling the agent, qualifying the interpretation of very low switch counts.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future public release; v2 reports that code, environments, datasets, oracle checkpoints, and a reproduction guide are available through the project site. This substantially changes the reported reproducibility resources. v2 also documents the timing-conversion assumptions and acknowledges IDRIS computing resources.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. Burda et al. and Yadgaroff et al. receive publication updates for already cited work, rather than becoming new references.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, standardizes MET terminology, divides Appendix C into subsections, and adds acknowledgements and a limitations heading. The publication header changes, but most prose and the main narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 6–8 are repositioned or resized, algorithm blocks are reformatted, and retained trajectory images are cropped. Appendix Figures 10 and 11 exchange numbering and placement. New Tables 4–5 and MET plots, an expanded intervention-panel arrangement, and removal of the old comparison figures substantially revise the displays.

improvement.justification: The broader MET controls and expert-time accounting make the existing expert-burden evidence more informative. Numerical uncertainty, specific applicability limits, and reported public resources improve transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of the matched-switch analyses, undefined ± quantities, and the conflicting Lazy-DAgger Maze scores in Tables 1 and 4. Overall, v2 provides a limited net improvement to an already substantial empirical study.
